prize_parts.citation: For an oeuvre that renews lyric, essay and narrative through a long, searching dialogue with antiquity, and that makes the book itself a form of elegy and thought, joining exacting learning to exposed feeling.

statement.case_for: My configuration does not change: Anne Carson (B002) as the single laureate. What changed after round 1 is how I would defend her. The six matching first places carry no weight with me, and I would not let them stand in for argument. The case rests on the writing. Her voice is recognisable within a few lines. In Autobiography of Red and Nox the formal decisions carry the emotional and intellectual meaning, so the form is the argument and not an ornament. Loss, desire, inheritance and the limits of translation recur across verse novel, lyric essay, drama and versions from Greek, and that recurrence is what sustained quality looks like in this oeuvre. I now state the core of the citation more narrowly than before. The credited core is her own writing: the verse novel, the lyric essay and the elegiac book-object. Translations and classical scholarship are context. Because Sem-Sandberg is right that translation is part of the elegiac method in Nox, the wording should say 'dialogue with antiquity' and not 'translator' or 'classicist'. I also want the citation to name the seriousness about grief and desire, so that it cannot be read as a prize for erudition alone. On the chair's question about later development, I should be honest. I can point to the Geryon material being taken up again in a later book (Red Doc>) and to her continued experiments with the book as an object. I cannot say from public knowledge, and without having verified those texts, whether these deepen the project or repeat it. I therefore rest the maturity claim on decades of recurring concerns together with repeated reinvention of the book as a form. I do not rest it on a demonstrated late phase. Where Carson can be read directly in English, my confidence rests on text I can weigh myself. That is a point about evidence, not a merit argument, and I do not count it as one.
statement.case_against: The reservations from round 1 stand and I have not resolved them. Part of the effect lives in page design, typography, Greek allusion and object-like presentation, and these may travel unevenly into Swedish and other languages. The line between scholarship, translation and literary achievement is a judgment call, and several of her books are short or fragmentary in scale. The chair's question about development after Nox is one I cannot answer with confidence. If a close reading by colleagues showed the later books refining an established method and not extending it, I would count that against the maturity case, as Mattson proposes. I would then take Cărtărescu or Zurita more seriously. I would not take them up merely because a prize might sit more comfortably with larger architecture. I would do it only if their cumulative achievement proved to be the sturdier whole-oeuvre claim. My alternatives are also weakly held. My own argument that I cannot judge Cărtărescu's Romanian applies equally to Zurita's Spanish, so my ordering of B005 before B042 is not a firm literary judgment.

responses.point: Olsson asked colleagues who know the Greek and English texts best to say, before a vote, whether the poems still work as poems for a reader without the classical sources, and proposed that the allusive apparatus is the material the poems transform.
responses.response: I take up that request as far as my own reading allows. I read Autobiography of Red as a modern love story that stands without Stesichorus, and Nox as a book of grief that stands without Catullus. The source extends the work and is not a condition of entering it. I hold this as my reading and not as a verified finding. I would add one condition to your point about an agreed citation text. It should make 'her own writing' the credited core, so that the allusive apparatus is named as material the writing transforms and is not credited as scholarship in its own right.

responses.point: Mattson says continuing invention in later work should be established openly, and that if it cannot be shown it should count against Carson. She also records doubt about whether Can Xue's single uncompromising method renews itself across books, having ranked her eighth where I ranked her third.
responses.response: I accept your standard on development. An unverified late phase should be stated as an unresolved gap and not assumed, and I have changed my wording accordingly. On Can Xue, your doubt and my opening ranking are less far apart than the ranks suggest. I placed her third for the uncompromising consistency of her method. I share your worry that consistency is a virtue only if the method keeps discovering something, and I cannot test that across her books from the translated sample. I do not propose her as a primary or alternative configuration, because that question is open for me too.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg argues that in Nox translation is itself the elegiac method, so it cannot simply be set aside as secondary. He also notes that direct assessment of poetry holds for Carson in English but much less for Zurita or Adonis, whose achievement lies in Spanish and Arabic prosody.
responses.response: Your point on Nox changes my wording and not my scope. The citation should not exclude translation as method, but it should credit the elegy as her own composition, with the translating act as part of its form. On evidence access, I agree it is a legitimate consideration and not a decisive one. Your point also exposes an inconsistency in my round-1 argument. I weighed my inability to judge Cărtărescu's Romanian against him, yet the same limit applies to Zurita, whom I ranked higher. I therefore hold my alternative ordering loosely. It rests on Zurita's moral and formal scale as I can perceive it, not on a firmer command of the Spanish.

responses.point: Carlberg disagreed with my ordering of Zurita and Can Xue above Cărtărescu, saying the question of whether Can Xue's sameness limits development is less settled than the case for Cărtărescu's late expansion. She also argued that Zurita's rootedness in one historical context raises a question about how it travels.
responses.response: The disagreement is fair, and the late expansion of Cărtărescu, with Solenoid as the example, is a real maturity argument that I cannot dismiss. I keep Zurita ahead of him as an alternative only narrowly. My reason is that the sequences carry their historical context into the form itself, as memorial writing, so I read the rootedness as the source of their force and not as a barrier to travel. I accept that this reading needs to be tested against the Spanish. On Can Xue, I now agree that the development question is unsettled and that she is not an alternative I would bring forward.

responses.point: Palm finds Zurita's landscape and sky-writing interventions a harder claim to make for a literary prize, while accepting my view that they belong to the poetry and not to separate artworks. She also calls fragmentary scale the main weighing for Carson's maturity.
responses.response: I would narrow my own claim for Zurita to match your doubt. The case for him should rest on the printed sequences, Purgatory and Anteparadise, with the landscape works treated as documented extensions that are not the core of a citation. On scale, I stay with my round-1 position. Sustained quality is not volume, but it needs visible recurrence and development, and I have said plainly that I cannot prove the development beyond Nox. Your caution is the strongest form of the objection, and it is the reason I treat my confidence in the maturity case as moderate and not high.

uncertainties: Whether Carson's later books (Red Doc> and the more object-like or performance-based work) deepen the project or refine an established method. I have not verified these texts and cannot establish this from public knowledge.

How much of the effect of Nox and similar works depends on typography, layout and book design that cannot be judged from text alone, and whether it survives translation into Swedish and other languages.
Where the line falls between literary achievement and scholarship or translation, and how a citation should treat translation as method in Nox.
Whether the committee reads a hybrid scholar-poet oeuvre as fitting Nobel's will and the 'ideal direction' criterion. I read it as imaginative and humane depth, but the question is open.

Translation and corpus coverage for the alternatives. I cannot judge Zurita's Spanish or Cărtărescu's dense Romanian prose, and his poetry is thinly translated. My ordering of B005 before B042 is therefore weakly held.
Each shortlist entry lists only two representative works, so any claim about a whole oeuvre rests on general public knowledge and not on verified reading.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. It lists committee colleagues and institutional programmes but no tie to Anne Carson or to any other shortlisted writer. My own practice as a novelist, and my stated interest in the global literary map and in female authorship, are context only. They are not evidence of a preference for any candidate and I do not rely on them.
